draft.title: Referendums
card: The Constitution is the set of rules that sets up Australia's government. It can be changed only by a referendum, which is a vote of all enrolled voters.
Parliament first passes a bill that proposes the change. Then voters are asked to answer yes or no to it.
To pass, a referendum needs a double majority. First, a majority of voters across the whole nation must vote yes.
Second, a majority of voters must vote yes in at least four of the six states. Voters in the territories count in the national total only.
draft.remember: A referendum passes only with a national majority and a majority in at least four states.

a.q: Which result would meet the double majority test for a referendum to pass?
opts: A national yes majority and yes majorities in four states
A national yes majority and yes majorities in two states
Yes majorities in four states but a national no majority
A yes majority in the House and in the Senate
a.why: The double majority has two parts: a majority of all voters and a majority in at least four states. Two states is not enough, and a House and Senate vote is how Parliament passes bills, not how voters change the Constitution.
a.clue: Both tests must be met at the same time.

b.q: A proposed change gets a yes vote from 55% of voters nationally, but only three states vote yes. What is the result?
opts: It fails, as only three states voted yes
It passes, as a national majority voted yes
It passes, as three states is nearly enough
It goes back to Parliament, which can then pass it
b.why: A national majority is only one of the two tests. A majority in at least four states is also needed, and three is not enough. So the change fails, however large the national yes vote is.
b.clue: Check both tests, not just the national vote.

a.best: A national yes majority and yes majorities in four states

b.best: It fails, as only three states voted yes
